items.title: Section: Three Ways of Eating, from Gluttony towards Freedom

items.zh: 復有三人。一者、有人貪染而食，愛著、饕餮乃至耽湎，不見過患、不知出離。二者、有人思擇而食，不染不著，亦不饕餮、吞吸、迷悶、堅住、耽湎，深見過患，善知出離，而於此食未斷未知。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person. First, one who eats with greed and attachment, indulging and gorging without restraint, seeing no fault in it and knowing nothing of freedom from it. Second, one who eats after reflection, without craving or clinging or gorging, deeply seeing the fault in it and knowing well the freedom from it, yet not having severed craving for this food or fully understood it. Third, one who eats after reflection, giving rise to no craving at all, deeply seeing the fault in it and knowing well the freedom from it, and having already severed craving for this food and fully understood it.

items.title: Section: Freedom from Food, and the Fragrance of a Gift

items.zh: 三者、有人思擇而食，不生貪染，廣說乃至深見過患，善知出離，又於此食已斷已知。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。復依施物說有三人。一者、有人所施之物，但具妙香，不具美妙味之與觸；二者、有人所施之物，具妙香味，而無妙觸；三者、有人所施之物，具足美妙香味與觸。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: Third, one who eats after reflection, giving rise to no craving, deeply seeing the fault and knowing the freedom from it, and having already severed craving for this food and fully understood it. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There are also three kinds of person by the object given: one whose gift possesses wonderful fragrance alone, without wonderful taste or texture; one whose gift possesses wonderful fragrance and taste, without wonderful texture; one whose gift possesses wonderful fragrance, taste, and texture all together. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: To Whom One Gives, and With What Kind of Heart

items.zh: 又依施田說有三人。一者、有人於愛於恩而行惠施；二者、有人於貧苦田而行惠施；三者、有人於具功德最勝福田而行惠施。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。復有差別。施於所愛名為下士，施於有恩名為中士，施於貧苦、具德勝田名為上士。又依施心說有三人。一者、有人將欲惠施，先心歡喜，正惠施時心不清淨，惠施已後尋復追悔；二者、有人先心歡喜，施時心淨，施已追悔；三者、有人先心歡喜，施時心淨，施已無悔。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person by the field given to: one who gives to those they love or to whom they owe gratitude; one who gives to the field of the poor and suffering; one who gives to the field complete with virtue, the most excellent field. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There is also a further distinction: giving to the loved is a lower person, giving to benefactors is a middling person, giving to the poor and suffering or to the field complete with virtue is a superior person. There are also three kinds of person by the mind in giving: one who feels joy beforehand, impurity of mind during the giving, and regret afterwards; one who feels joy beforehand, purity of mind during the giving, yet regret afterwards; one who feels joy beforehand, purity of mind during the giving, and no regret afterwards. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: The Merit of Upholding Precepts, Complete or Lacking

items.zh: 復於受持戒福業事建立三人。一者、有人但離一分，非一切時常能遠離，唯自遠離，不勸他離，亦不讚美，見同法者心不歡喜，是名下士。二者、有人離一切分，一切時離，唯自遠離，不勸他人，亦不讚美，見同法者心不歡喜，是名中士。三者、有人一切俱現，是名上士。又於受持禁戒處所建立三人。一者、有人住惡說法毘奈耶中受持禁戒；二者、有人住善說法毘奈耶中受持禁戒，而有缺漏；三者、有人即住於此受持禁戒，而不缺漏。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person by the merit-deed of upholding precepts. One who abstains from only a portion, not constantly, alone and without encouraging or praising others, taking no joy in a fellow practitioner's observance, is a lower person. One who abstains entirely and constantly, yet still alone, without encouraging or praising others, taking no joy in a fellow practitioner's observance, is a middling person. One in whom all of this is fully present is a superior person. There are also three kinds of person by the place of upholding precepts. One who upholds precepts within a wrongly taught doctrine and discipline; one who upholds precepts within the well-taught doctrine and discipline, yet with lapses; one who upholds precepts within that same doctrine and discipline, without lapse. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: Why One Takes Precepts, and What Kind One Takes

items.zh: 又於受持戒心建立三人。一者、有人為活命故，受持禁戒；二者、有人為生天故，受持禁戒；三者、有人為涅槃故，受持禁戒。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又於受持別解脫律儀說有三人。一者、有人唯能受持近住律儀；二者、有人亦能受持近事律儀；三者、有人亦能受持苾芻律儀。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person by the mind in taking precepts. One who takes precepts for the sake of livelihood; one who takes precepts for the sake of heavenly rebirth; one who takes precepts for the sake of nirvana. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There are also three kinds of person by the prātimokṣa restraint upheld. One who can uphold only the one-day restraint; one who can also uphold the lay restraint; one who can also uphold the monastic restraint. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: The Four Supports of a True Monastic

items.zh: 又於受持苾芻律儀說有三人。一者、有人唯能成就受具足支，無受隨法諸學處支，亦無隨護他人心支，亦無隨護如先所受諸學處支。二者、有人成前三支，無後一支。三者、有人具成四支。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person by monastic restraint upheld. One who achieves only the support of full ordination, without the support of the further training rules, without the support of guarding others' minds, and without the support of guarding the training rules already received. One who achieves the first three supports, without the fourth. One complete in all four supports. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

items.title: Section: Three Restraints, and All That One Has Received

items.zh: 又有三人。一者、有人唯成別解脫律儀；二者、有人成別解脫、靜慮律儀；三者、有人成別解脫、靜慮、無漏三種律儀。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又有三人。一者、有人唯能成就非律儀非不律儀攝所受戒律儀；二者、有人亦能成就聲聞等相應所受戒律儀；三者、有人亦能成就菩提薩埵所受戒律儀。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person. One who achieves only prātimokṣa restraint; one who achieves prātimokṣa and meditative restraint; one who achieves prātimokṣa, meditative, and undefiled restraint, all three. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. There are also three kinds of person. One who achieves only the restraint received that is neither restraint nor non-restraint; one who also achieves the restraint received corresponding to the śrāvaka path; one who also achieves the restraint received of a bodhisattva.

blocks.text: More sets of three persons: how they eat, how they give, how they keep precepts.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the middle person only subdues craving for food without knowing its seeds remain; the best has severed the seeds and eats only to practise.
The best gift has fragrance, taste, and pleasant touch together.

subs.head: To whom, and with what heart

blocks.text: Giving to the poor, who truly need it, is "timely" and superior. All three givers are glad beforehand; the first is impure while giving, the second regrets afterwards, the third has no regret.
Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing others keep precepts and not rejoicing is the lower person.
Master Cháng Bǎi: keeping the eight precepts for one day and night is the lower grade; adding the five lay precepts for life is higher.
Master Cháng Bǎi: without guarding others' minds one lacks perfect conduct.
Master Cháng Bǎi: meditative restraint subdues afflictions; the noble path severs their seeds. Ordinary conduct belongs to neither vow: good or evil arising with circumstances.
Three givers, all glad beforehand; only one is glad afterwards too. The test of a gift is how one feels after giving it.

quiz.q: What does the second person, who eats after reflection, still lack?
options: affliction over food is only subdued; its seeds remain and its fault is not yet truly known
the person still craves while eating and merely pretends not to
the person has not taken precepts
the person has not ordained
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this person only subdues the affliction over food, without yet knowing fully that its seeds remain, or truly knowing the fault. The third person has severed those seeds and knows the fault. The line between them lies in severing.

quiz.q: This is rendered "having already severed and fully realised this freedom." Why is the sense reversed?
options: it is not reversed, since to sever means to achieve, as the lecture says
it should be "eaten this food"
"already" should be deleted
what is severed and known is food, whereas the English says the freedom itself is severed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: taking food only for practice, this person has severed the seeds of greed and truly knows the fault of craving food. The object is food or craving for it. Read literally, the English has the person severing freedom itself.

quiz.q: By the object given, what is the superior person's gift like?
options: it has wonderful fragrance, taste, and texture
only fragrance, the purest of the three, ranking first
fragrance and taste only
gold and silver of top value
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the third person's gift has wonderful fragrance, taste, and touch together, and this is a superior person. The ranking simply counts qualities: fragrance alone is lower, and with taste is middling. Monetary value is not mentioned.

quiz.q: 於愛於恩 is rendered "gives out of love or gratitude." What is wrong?
options: nothing: they are donor's feelings and the heading is misplaced, as the lecture corrects
this list is by field, so 愛 and 恩 are recipients, whereas the English makes them motives
it should be "anger"
it should be "fear"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one gives to beloved wife and children, and to parents and teachers who have shown kindness. These are recipients. The English heading says "by the field given to," and "out of" collapses this list into the next one on the giver's mind.

quiz.q: By the mind in giving, at which stage do the second and third persons differ?
options: after giving: the second regrets it, and the third does not regret it at all
before giving: the second is not glad and the third is, the prior mind counting most
during giving: the second is impure and the third pure
there is no difference
quiz.why: All three are glad beforehand. The first is impure during giving, the second pure but regretful afterwards, and the third free of regret. Master Cháng Bǎi: after giving this person does not look back in regret, since giving completes merit.

quiz.q: In the "further distinction" of the field, where does giving to the poor belong, and how does this differ from the first list?
options: lower in both, the poor being no field of merit, so the text is consistent throughout
middling in both
middling in the second list
superior in the second list, whereas in the first it is middling; they are two classifications
quiz.why: Giving to the poor shifts rank between lists. Master Cháng Bǎi: giving to the poor, who truly need the goods, is timely giving, and in this second scheme it is superior. Any answer must say which classification is meant.

quiz.q: What marks the lower person in the merit-deed of keeping precepts?
options: abstaining partly and not always, alone, without urging or praising others, and not rejoicing in fellow practitioners
abstaining fully and always, urging and praising others, and rejoicing, all merely outward goodness
not taking precepts at all
taking outside precepts
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing fellow precept-holders do the merit-deed of keeping precepts, this person does not know to rejoice, and is called a lower person. Option B describes the superior person's full presence of all these qualities.

quiz.q: Why, per Master Cháng Bǎi, does lay restraint rank above one-day restraint?
options: the lay restraint has more rules, eight against five, and the number sets the rank
the first is for monastics
the eight-precept restraint lasts only one day and night, while the five precepts are kept for life
the first is for women only
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first person keeps only the eight-precept observance for one day and night, a short time, and is lower. The second also keeps the five lay precepts, held for life, and is middling. Duration is the reason given.

quiz.q: What does a monk with only the support of full ordination lack, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: nothing: the ordination ceremony completes everything, so this person is superior
the tonsure ceremony
lay offerings
the further training rules, guarding others' minds through proper conduct, and fearing even minor faults
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: without the support of guarding others' minds one lacks perfect conduct and observance of the rules against public censure; without the last, one does not see great fear in minor faults. Ordination alone makes only a lower person.

quiz.q: By the three restraints, how is the superior person identified?
options: prātimokṣa alone, since precepts are the root and the others are incidental
prātimokṣa and meditative restraint
achieving prātimokṣa, meditative, and undefiled restraint, all three
undefiled restraint alone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: meditative restraint has power to subdue afflictions, and with meditation the desire-realm afflictions do not arise; the noble path then severs their seeds, so the precepts become truly and finally pure. So each added restraint deepens purity.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the restraint that is neither restraint nor non-restraint?
options: neither the highest good of Buddhist restraint nor the extreme evil of non-restraint, but the middling good and evil arising with conditions
the bodhisattva precepts, which transcend both categories and are kept for all time
the monastic precepts
the evil restraint
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this refers to neither the extreme good of Buddhist restraint nor the extreme evil of non-restraint, but good or evil arising with circumstances. The bodhisattva precepts are held by the third person, vowed for all future time.
